questions.prompt: Which loops never end by themselves (without a `break`)?
questions.explain: `for (;;)` and `while (1)` have no false condition; the third loop never changes `i`. `while (0)` never runs at all.
option_notes: The condition is false at once: zero passes.

questions.prompt: A {{0}} loop tests its condition after the body, so the body always runs at least once.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a `for (init; cond; update) body` loop in the order they happen.
questions.explain: `init` runs once; then the cycle is: test the condition, run the body, run the update, test again... until the condition is false.
items: the body runs (if cond was true)

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `int a[5]; for (int i = 0; i <= 5; i++) a[i] = 0;`?
questions.explain: An array of 5 elements has the indices 0 to 4. `i <= 5` visits index 5: an off-by-one error that corrupts memory.
options: It writes a[5], one element past the end of the array (undefined behaviour)
`i` must be declared before the loop
option_notes: It also writes outside the array.
Declaring `i` in the `for` is allowed in C99.
